patches.old: The SA node has an intrinsic depolarization rate of approximately 60–100 bpm, but this rate is continuously modulated by the autonomic nervous system.
patches.new: The SA node's intrinsic rate (measured with autonomic input blocked) is roughly 100–110 bpm in young adults, but this rate is continuously modulated by the autonomic nervous system; resting heart rate is normally 60–100 bpm.
patches.reason: Intrinsic SA-node rate is ~100–110 bpm; 60–100 bpm is the normal resting rate after vagal tone.

patches.old: This produces a **negative chronotropic effect** by increasing potassium conductance (IKACh), hyperpolarizing the cell and slowing phase 4 depolarization.
patches.new: This produces a **negative chronotropic effect** by increasing potassium conductance (IK,ACh), which hyperpolarizes the cell, and by decreasing the funny current (If) and L-type calcium current, which together slow phase 4 depolarization.
patches.reason: ACh also reduces If and ICa; completes the mechanism.

patches.old: increasing parasympathetic tone and decreasing HR (the **Bezold-Jarisch** and **baroreflex** responses)
patches.new: increasing parasympathetic tone and decreasing HR (the **baroreceptor reflex**). The Bezold-Jarisch reflex is a different reflex, triggered by cardiac (mainly ventricular) receptors, that causes bradycardia and hypotension
patches.reason: Bezold-Jarisch is a cardiopulmonary chemoreceptor reflex, not the arterial baroreflex.

patches.old: the "atrial kick" contributes ~20–30% of ventricular filling, which is lost in atrial fibrillation
patches.new: the "atrial kick" adds the final portion of ventricular filling—commonly taught as ~20–30%, though estimates run from ~10% at rest to much more at high heart rates—and it is lost in atrial fibrillation
patches.reason: Sources differ (OpenStax 20–30%; Klabunde ~10% at rest, up to 40% at high rates); present the range honestly.

patches.old: intracellular Na⁺ rises → Na⁺/Ca²⁺ exchanger (NCX) runs in reverse → intracellular Ca²⁺ rises → increased contractility
patches.new: intracellular Na⁺ rises → the smaller Na⁺ gradient slows Ca²⁺ removal by the Na⁺/Ca²⁺ exchanger (NCX) → intracellular and SR Ca²⁺ rise → increased contractility
patches.reason: The accepted mechanism is reduced forward-mode Ca²⁺ efflux, not wholesale reversal of NCX.

patches.old: - **Digoxin** increases contractility by inhibiting Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase → elevated intracellular Na⁺ → reverse NCX → elevated intracellular Ca²⁺
patches.new: - **Digoxin** increases contractility by inhibiting Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase → elevated intracellular Na⁺ → less Ca²⁺ extruded by NCX → elevated intracellular Ca²⁺
patches.reason: Same NCX correction in the summary.

patches.old: - **Parasympathetic stimulation** decreases HR (no significant direct effect on contractility)
patches.new: - **Parasympathetic stimulation** decreases HR and slows AV conduction (little direct effect on ventricular contractility, because vagal fibers mainly supply the atria and nodes)
patches.reason: Clarifies that vagal effects on contractility are minor for the ventricles specifically.

patches.old: increased contractility steepens ESPVR and narrows loop leftward
patches.new: increased contractility steepens ESPVR, lowers ESV, and widens the loop (larger SV)
patches.reason: Increased inotropy decreases ESV and increases SV, so the loop gets wider, not narrower.

visual.title: How preload and contractility change stroke volume
visual.alt: Left: Frank-Starling curves of stroke volume against end-diastolic volume; increased contractility gives a higher curve and heart failure a lower curve, while a preload change moves along one curve. Right: pressure-volume loops; increased contractility steepens the end-systolic pressure-volume line, lowers end-systolic volume and widens the loop.
visual.caption: Schematic, not patient data. Stroke volume is the loop's width (EDV − ESV). Raising afterload would instead raise the loop and increase ESV, narrowing it.
